newsitem.title: USA: NCAA BASKETBALL-KENTUCKY PRESSURE IS ARIZONA'S TOP OBSTACLE TO TITLE.
newsitem.headline: NCAA BASKETBALL-KENTUCKY PRESSURE IS ARIZONA'S TOP OBSTACLE TO TITLE.

text.p: Kentucky players know what their fullcourt, all-game-long pressure defence does to opponents.
"The big thing we look for is when they are bending over, grabbing their shorts and gasping," guard Anthony Epps said.

And when the opponents relievedly go to the sidelines during a timeout, Epps knows what they're thinking: "'I've got to go out and face that press again' -- instead of listening to what their coach says."
"There's a huge mental aspect of the game to fight through the fatigue," said senior forward Jared Prickett. "You're tired but you see your opponent is twice as tired.
"It's a great feeling when you're on defence to see that the other team is so confused. It's chaos out there, and they don't know where you're coming from or where the next shot is coming from."

Arizona coach Lute Olson sees the Kentucky pressure as obstacle number one in Monday night's collegiate basketball championship game, but believes his starting trio of good ball-handling guards can cope with it.

"Obviously, in playing them it begins and ends, probably, with dealing with their fullcourt pressure. But I think one of our strengths is the fact that we have three guards who can handle, and plus Jason Terry coming off the bench.
"And I feel comfortable with the ability of our big people to catch (the ball) and find open people as well."
Olson predicted a fast-paced game to both teams' liking and added: "I'm not going to say it's going to be easy, because it's not. Their pressure is relentless."
Arizona's young frontcourt players sounded confident.
"When teams try to press us, we've broken the press almost every time and they've had to back off the press," said freshman phenomenon Mike Bibby.
"They're a great team and they have a great press," said Michael Dickerson. "But I think we have the players to break that press.
"I feel good. I'm not scared of them," said team leader Miles Simon. "If we beat the pressure, it's just going to be easier shots for us down at the other end of the court."

Simon pointed out the success South Carolina's three-guard offence had in beating Kentucky twice this season. "I think our guards have the same capability as those guards, and I think we can cause them a lot of problems."
Kentucky point guard Wayne Turner conceded the quick South Carolina guard threesome had "showed us our weakness" and sent the Wildcats back to "work on the things we need to work on."
Said Epps: "We're going to take it as a positive, not as a negative."
Arizona centre A.J. Bramlett said never mind the guards, it's the frontcourt that will make the difference.
"They have great perimeter players in Turner, (Ron) Mercer and Epps but I think our perimeter matches up with theirs. How we handle the pressure depends on the big men."
Against Arizona's quicker frontcourt, Kentucky forward Scott Padgett said, "The key will be our big guys. They have to sprint like they've never sprinted this year."
All the Kentucky players say they practice so hard against the press, real games are easy by comparison. And the defending national champions say other teams just think they're pressing fullcourt.

"I think our press is a lot different from everyone else," said Prickett. "Some teams will trap you once, then if you make the pass, they'll fall back. With us we trap and if you make the pass, we trap again. Make the pass and we'll trap again, and we may trap you after you cross halfcourt.
"We're coming at you all the time."

"The last two years our defence has maintained the level of excellence at each level of the floor," said Pitino. "When they cross halfcourt our defence gets just as strong with our man-to-man, and I think that's key.
But the Kentucky coach said that where in Saturday's semifinal win his team had keyed on Minnesota's top two scorers, Bobby Jackson and Sam Jacobson, it could not against more versatile Arizona.

"Right now there's no question in my mind that our press tomorrow is not going to have the same success it had against Minnesota, playing against Arizona with the ball-handling ability that they have," said Pitino.
"We're going to have to mix up our defences tomorrow."

Arizona has not seen a full-blown pressure defence this season. "No one in the Pac 10, I don't think anyone really all year pressed us," said Simon. "Our scout team will pressure us and will probably have six or seven guys on the floor to match Kentucky's quickness."

Olson said Arizona aimed to stay aggressive against the press. "I've always felt that (if) somebody presses, we're going right at them, because otherwise you let them take all kinds of gambles and you don't burn them. We have not been a team that a lot of teams have chosen to press through the years.
"And I think part of it is the fact that they know we're not just going to get through the press and stop, we're going to go to the hole."
